Brief Hospital Course:
A ___ year old lady with DMI and known gastroparesis presenting 
with another episode of gastroparesis as nausea and vomiting 
without a clear inciting factor. Was admitted, giving IV 
medications, IVF, and transitioned back to regular diet and PO 
medications with the resolution of nausea.
.  
1) Gastroparesis: secondary to diabetes type 1, consistent with 
dysautomonia and other pheripheral neruopathies. Patient had had 
previous admissions for this in the past and has a gatric 
pacemaker placed as a result.  Patient was given IV anti-emetics 
and was supported with IVF. Standing Zofran and metoclopromide, 
Ativan, Compazine PRN. Diet was advanced to regular and the 
patient was tolerating PO medications at the time of discharge. 
Gastric pacemaker appears to be working properly and will be 
interogated as an outpatient by Dr. ___.
.  
2) Type I Diabetes mellitus: The patient has complicated 
diabetes with current poor glycemic control with BS in the 200s 
despite not taking PO. When given same scale in house, control 
was excellent. Started on ASA 81mg PO daily and Lisinopril 2.5mg 
PO daily for management of diabteics nephropathy and 
microalbuminuria.
.  
3) Abnormal Cardiac Enzymes: Despite lack of chest pain and 
significant EKG changes, the patient's MB fraction is abnormally 
elevated. Appears to be lab anamaoly, repeat labs normal. Of no 
clinical significant.
.

Discharge Instructions:
You have been admitted to the hospital with an episode of 
gastroparesis, nausea and vomiting.  While you were here we were 
able to control your symptoms with IV medications and fluids.  
At the time of discharge, you were tolerating a regular diet and 
PO medications.

You are to start a baby aspirin to protect your heart from an 
attack. You are to start taking lisinopril to protect your 
kidney from diabetes damage. You are being given  anti-nausea 
medication that you can take as needed.

If you develop worsening nausea or vomiting, fever, chest pain, 
difficulty breathing, abdominal pain or any other concerning 
medical symptom, please call your doctor or 911.
